0. FOREWORD
Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 September 1986, after the draft finalized by the Natural and Synthetic Perfumery Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 This Indian Standard was first published in 1966. The Sectional Committee responsible for its preparation felt that it should be revised with a view to bring it in line with trade practices in perfumery technology and also to align with the quality of the material currently manufactured and sold in the country. 0.3 Styralyl acetate ( CroHr20, ) is from Gardenia spp fam. Rubiaceae. fumery chemical used extensively in in tuberose, jasmine and other floral structural formula: found in the oil of gardenia flower It is a commercially available pergardenia scents and to some extent compositions. It has the following

Requirements of relative density and refractive index have also been modified. 3

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4.1 The material shall be supplied in glass bottles, or in any suitable container as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

GAS CHROMATOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS FOR DETERMINATION OF STYRALYL ACETATE A-O. GENERAL A-0.1 The chromatographic conditions given here are for guidance only.

A-O.2 Outline of the Method - A sample of th.e material is injected into the gas chromatograph where it is carried by the carrier gas from one end of the column to the other. During its movement, constituents of the sample undergo distribution at different rates and ultimately get separated from one another. The separated constituents emerge from the end of the column one after another and are detected by suitable means whose response is related to the amount of a specific component leaving the column.

A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Conduct the flow of the carrier gas and inject the sample at inject port where it is vaporized and well-mixed with the carrier. This is led into the chromatographic column wherein vaporized constituents of the sample are separated out by virtue of their differing interaction with the stationary phase. As the different constituents pass through the detector, they give signals corresponding to the amount of particular constituent leaving the column. The detector signal, on transmission to the recorder, plots the chart. From the specific area under various peaks correspondthe quantities of different constituents are ing to specific constituents, determined.
NOTE - For the separation maintained at the temperature tion of the constituents. to be efficient, it is necessary that the column is suggested throughout the time required for resolu-

IS : 3928 - 1986 A-3. CALCULATION A-3.1 Area Measurement ( seeNote 1) - Since normal peaks approximate a triangle, the area is measured by multiplying the peak height with the width of half-height. The normal -peak. base is not taken. since large deviations may be observed due to tailing or adsorption. This technique is rapid, simple and fairly accurate when peaks are symmetrical and are of reasonable width. A-3.2 Area Normalization ( see Note 2 ) - By normalization, it is meant, calculating the percentage composition by measuring the area of each and dividing the individual.areas by total area, for example: Percentage Area of A x 1OO of A = Total area

NOTE1 -Other methods of area measurement, namely, triangulation disc integrator and electronic digital integrator, if fixed with GLC machine, would be of great advantage.

can be used if pure appropriate internal Nope 2 - Imernal standardization standard is available. This method is known as relative or indirect calibration.
